def test_correct_bracketing():

    assert correct_bracketing("") == True          # empty string is balanced
    assert correct_bracketing("<>") == True        # simple pair
    assert correct_bracketing("<<>>") == True      # nested brackets
    assert correct_bracketing("<><>") == True      # sequential pairs
    assert correct_bracketing("<<<>>>") == True    # triple nesting
    assert correct_bracketing("<<><>>") == True    # mixed nesting

    # Invalid cases
    assert correct_bracketing(">") == False        # closing before opening
    assert correct_bracketing("<") == False        # unclosed opening bracket
    assert correct_bracketing("><") == False       # closing first
    assert correct_bracketing("<<") == False       # two unclosed brackets
    assert correct_bracketing(">>") == False       # two closings, no opening
    assert correct_bracketing("<<>") == False      # missing one closing
    assert correct_bracketing("<>>") == False      # extra closing
    assert correct_bracketing("<><>>") == False    # unbalanced at end
    assert correct_bracketing("<><") == False      # unclosed at end
    assert correct_bracketing("<<><") == False     # nested but unclosed
    assert correct_bracketing("<><><") == False    # sequence ending unclosed

    # Edge case: goes negative mid-string even if it would balance later
    assert correct_bracketing(">><<") == False

def correct_bracketing(brackets: str):
    depth = 0
    for b in brackets:
        if b == "<":
            depth += 1
        else:
            depth -= 1
        if depth < 0:
            return False
    return depth == 0
